Do you hear that? The constant gunfire? The shelling? And they tell the world there is a ceasefire? There is no pause. No reprieve. No safety for Palestinians in Gaza. On October 11, our team visited families whose tents had been burned, leaving them without shelter once again. Even as we filmed, heavy gunfire echoed around us. This is the reality of life in Gaza. Families who have lost everything continue to live under the threat of violence, yet refuse to be driven from their land. This is what steadfastness looks like. Sumud. A determination that is difficult to comprehend unless you understand what it means to face the loss of your homeland. They have burned their shelters, destroyed their neighborhoods, and displaced them again and again. But they have not broken their connection to Palestine. They are not leaving. They are not surrendering their right to exist on their land. Help support them. The Sameer Project is one of the only organizations that delivers aid in these danger zones. They aren’t playing. They aren’t looking for lost toys. They’re searching for food. Two children, sitting in the garbage in Gaza, picking through things most of us wouldn’t even want to touch. And what makes this scene so painful is how quietly it’s happening. There’s no crowd gathered around them. No one stopping the world because two little children are hungry. Cars continue down the road. People go about their day. And these two remain on the ground, searching. I keep looking at that little girl’s hand. She’s holding a small piece of something while reaching for more. I wonder how hungry a child has to be before a pile of rubbish starts looking like a place where she might find something worth eating. Hunger has a way of stealing things long before it takes a life. It steals patience, energy, concentration, sleep. And in children, it steals the freedom to think about anything other than the next meal. What we’re witnessing here isn’t simply poverty. It’s the humiliation of having your most basic needs pushed so far out of reach that even discarded scraps become worth searching for. These children are sitting in the waste of a world that has more than enough to feed them. And perhaps that’s what makes this footage so difficult to watch. Not because their suffering is impossible to understand, but because it should never have been allowed to become ordinary. Their hunger is real. Their dignity is real. And neither should be buried beneath the world’s indifference. 🇵🇸💔 #palestine #gaza #fyp #freepalestine #humanity
